statements.impact_statement: OpenSSH host key handling use-after-free. The restic image carries the ssh client binaries in its alpine layer; our jobs use an S3 repository (no sftp backend) and never run ssh.
statements.action_statement: Re-check on restic 0.19.2 (the image was last built 2026-07-05; no fixed tag exists). Drop this statement once a fixed tag is pinned.

statements.impact_statement: Go crypto/tls session resumption in the kustomize binary bundled in the toolbox image. Our Jobs run kubectl, jq and curl, never kustomize.
statements.action_statement: Re-check on the next alpine/k8s tag (1.36.5 and 1.37.1 are the latest); consider a minimal kubectl image so unused tools are not shipped.

statements.impact_statement: PyJWT public key handling, pulled in by barman-cloud's Azure authentication path. We archive WAL to S3 and never configure Azure; nothing verifies a JWT with it.
statements.action_statement: No newer plain 18.x/16.x tag exists. Evaluate the -standard-trixie variant by a scan before the expiry.

statements.impact_statement: certifi bundles emSign roots whose intermediate CA keys leaked (fixed in certifi 2026.10.19). It is a dependency of Python tools in the toolbox image; our Jobs run kubectl, jq and curl, which use the system CA store, and never start Python.
statements.action_statement: Re-check on the next alpine/k8s tag (none carries certifi 2026.10.19 yet).

statements.impact_statement: certifi is only consulted by `requests`. In k8s-sidecar 2.14.1 `requests` calls only REQ_URL, and the Grafana chart sets it to http://localhost:3000 (plain HTTP, nothing to verify); the Kubernetes API client verifies against the ServiceAccount ca.crt (ssl_ca_cert), not certifi. Read in the image's sidecar.py, helpers.py and kubernetes/config/incluster_config.py, and in the rendered Grafana chart. Revisit if a sidecar URL annotation or an HTTPS REQ_URL is ever configured.
statements.action_statement: No newer k8s-sidecar tag exists (2.14.1 is the latest, 2026-10-08). Bump when one carries certifi 2026.10.19.

statements.impact_statement: Next.js 'use cache' functions returning typed arrays (next >= 16.0.0 and <= 16.4.0, App router with Cache Components). The Zitadel login build has cacheComponents, experimental.useCache and ppr set to false and no 'use cache' function in its server code (read from required-server-files.json and the built chunks of the v4.19.5 image pinned by digest; the only 'use cache' strings in the chunks are Next.js's own error messages, no directive was found).
statements.action_statement: A fixed image exists since 2026-11-03: zitadel-login v4.20.1 ships Next.js 16.4.3. It is not bumped in 0.4.2 (no runtime change). Bump zitadel and zitadel-login together in the next release that changes the runtime, prove it on a cluster, and drop this statement then.
statements.status_notes: Expires: 2026-12-04. Renewed 2026-11-04 (first recorded 2026-10-22) after re-reading the image: the pinned zitadel-login v4.19.5 still ships next 16.3.6, cacheComponents, useCache and ppr are still false, and the built code holds no 'use cache' directive.

statements.impact_statement: Next.js image optimization endpoint (libvips memory bug in sharp on glibc, fixed in sharp >= 0.35.5; next >= 16.0.0 and <= 16.4.0). The login image is built on node:24-alpine (musl) and ships sharp 0.35.4 with glibc binaries only (@img/sharp-linux-x64 and its libvips, no linuxmusl package): require('sharp') from Next.js's directory fails there ('Could not load the sharp module using the linuxmusl-x64 runtime', run on the pinned image) and Next.js 16 has no fallback, so the vulnerable code never loads. FRAGILE: it becomes reachable if the image is rebuilt on a glibc base. The Login V2 UI is routed through the Gateway since 0.4.0 (apps #161) and the optimizer path /ui/v2/login/_next/image is sent to the server, which answers 404, a rule that scripts/dev/test-zitadel-login-route.py keeps in place. The build also has dangerouslyAllowSVG false and no remotePattern; that is not the reason relied on here.
statements.action_statement: A fixed image exists since 2026-11-03: zitadel-login v4.20.1 ships Next.js 16.4.3 and sharp 0.35.5. It is not bumped in 0.4.2 (no runtime change). Bump zitadel and zitadel-login together in the next release that changes the runtime, prove it on a cluster, and drop this statement then. Re-check at once if the base image of the pinned tag changes.
